$note: Phase-3 blocks: four archetypes × three hand-authored levels (design D2: dual axes per archetype, ~1.3× per stat per level, cost matched to the compounded ~1.7× power so gold-per-output stays flat), real swarm/tank/runner stat blocks, and the reserved slow-immune brute (unused until Phase 4). Rows tuned against the leak-rate harness (tests/leak.test.ts): the rapid range came down from phase-2's 3.5 so one archetype can no longer cover both maze ends, and each enemy type's punisher pressure is asserted directionally there, not by feel. Balance-ux-tweaks pass: area damage down one step (L1 now 3-shots a 50hp swarm instead of 2), slow row rescaled from 60 and wall up to 20 so mazing itself carries real cost, waveBonus pays settlement gold that decays once a wave runs past its last scheduled spawn + grace (design D4) — replacing interest as the tempo incentive. Energy-infrastructure pass: every tower level carries a ratedPower and the power block below adds the standby fraction and the solar panel.

power.$note: Energy-infrastructure placeholders (design intent in the change proposal, tuning is balance authoring): standby is a small non-zero share so a wave is never free and a battery has a baseline to charge against; the panel is a deliberate investment — several walls' worth of gold, roughly two level-1 towers of output — so a few move the meter visibly and one competes with the next connection tier at a similar price. Rated power per level sits on the tower rows and grows slower than damage, so upgrading is power-efficient. The battery (capacity in kWh, one second of wave time being one hour) is sized so that one panel's quiet-tick surplus never fills it within a wave while two panels' does, and priced below the panel — it is the second purchase of a solar line, never the first.
